newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in thin session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in thin session.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Monday in a thinly traded session, reflecting varied trading in natural gas futures and the spot cash market in the western U.S.
"It's really quiet. We're really rangebound," said an East Coast paper broker.
There was little fresh fundamental news today to give the complex short-term direction, brokers and traders said.
March California-Oregion Border (COB) futures finished down five cents at $10.85 a megawatt hour (MWh), its session high after traded as low as $10,65.
April COB settled up five cents at $10.10. Other active COB contracts ended down 20 cents to up 15 cents.
March Palo Verde (PV) futues finished down 20 cents at $13.10 after bouncing in a 10 cent range.
April PV was quiet. Most other active PV months ended up five cents.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 1.5 cents at $2.167 per million British thermal units. April Hub gas finished up 1.5 cents at $2.107.
Firm, peak electricity prices at COB for day-ahead delivery fell $1.75 from Friday's levels, while those at PV held steady from Friday.
"I don't see too much change. There's no extreme weather coming," said a Denver-based trader when asked about Tuesday's activity.

Although there is no clear short-term direction of the power complex, the long-term outlook seems bearish with early evidence confirming worries over abundant sources for hydroelectric production in the West this spring.
The Northwest River Forecast Center confirmed preliminary forecasts for spring runoff of 137 percent of normal at The Dalles dam on the Columbia River in Oregon.
Separately, a 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico would likely back up Tuesday after tripping off line Sunday.
The 1,100 MW pumped storage hydroelectric Helms plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Feb 1 for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for another week.
In the Northwest, temeperatures will average near normal this week peaking in the 30-50s degrees F with near normal precipitation.
In the Southwest, readings will average slightly below normal this week with day temperatures hitting the 50-70 degree range. Snow showers are possible in New Mexico Tuesday.
NYMEX estimated 77 COB and 62 PV contracts were sold, down from Friday's sales of 79 COB and 269 PV lots.
